chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The endive is the chief of the vegetables.
ai.seo_question: What is the best vegetable according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates endive (hinda') to the status of 'chief of vegetables,' reflecting the Shia tradition of emphasizing practical health benefits (tibb) alongside spiritual well-being. This designation underscores the Prophetic emphasis on simple, nutritious foods as part of a balanced lifestyle, aligning with the broader Islamic ethic of valuing natural provisions as signs of divine mercy.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin sadaqa, from Ziyad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The endive is the chief of the vegetables’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Sadaqah from Ziyad who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The endive is the master of herbs.’”
